σκοτία.as:
† σκοτία, -ας, ἡ
[in LXX: Jb 28:3 (אֹפֶל), Mi 3:6 (חָשְׁכָה), Is 16:3 * ;]
in late writers = σκότος,
darkness: Jo 6:1720:1. Metaph.,
(a) of secrecy (opp. to ἐν τ. φωτί): Mt 10:27, Lk 12:3;
(b) of spiritual darkness: Mt 4:16, Jo 1:58:1212:35, 46, I Jo 1:52:8, 9, 11.†

σκιά.g: a shadow, thick darkness, an outline
σκιά.long: a shadow, shade, thick darkness, an outline.
σκιά.sd: "shade" or a shadow (literally or figuratively (darkness of error or an adumbration))
σκιά.as:
σκιά, -ᾶς, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for צֵל, IV Ki 20:9 ff., Ps 56 (57):1, al.; but σ. and σ. θανάτου are also used for צַלְמָוֶת, Jb 3:5, Ps 22 (23):4, Is 9:2 (1) (v. ICC, in l.), al. ;]
1.shadow, shade, caused by interception of light: Mk 4:32, Ac 5:15; metaph., σ. θανάτου, of ignorance and error, Mt 4:16, Lk 1:79(LXX).
2.a shadow, the image or outline cast by an object: fig., ὑπόδειγμα καὶ σ., He 8:5; opp. to σῶμα, Col 2:17; opp. to εἰκών, He 10:1.†

σκανδαλίζω.long: I cause to stumble, cause to sin, cause to become indignant, shock, offend.
σκανδαλίζω.sd: to entrap, i.e. trip up (figuratively, stumble (transitively) or entice to sin, apostasy or displeasure)
σκανδαλίζω.as:
† σκανδαλίζω
(< σκάνδαλον), [in LXX: Da LXX 11:41 (כּשׁל ni.), Si 9:535 (32):15 (יקשׁ ho.) ib. 23:8 (also in Aq., Sm., Th., and in Ps Sol 16:7; not elsewhere, except NT and eccl.)* ;]
prop., to put a snare or stumbling-block in the way; in NT always metaph. of that which hinders right conduct or thought, to cause to stumble: c. acc. pers., Mt 5:29, 3017:2718:6, 8, 9Mk 9:42, 43, 45, 47Lk 17:2, Jo 6:61, I Co 8:13. Pass., to be made to stumble, to stumble: Mt 11:613:21, 5715:1224:1026:31, 33, Mk 4:176:314:27, 29, Lk 7:23, Jo 16:1, Ro 14:21 (WH, R, txt., om.), II Co 11:29,†

σκυθρωπός.sd: angry-visaged, i.e. gloomy or affecting a mournful appearance
σκυθρωπός.der: from (sullen) and a derivative of G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι);
σκυθρωπός.as:
σκυθρωπός, -όν (also -ή, -όν)
(< σκυθρός, sullen, + ὤψ), [in LXX: Ge 40:7 (רַע), etc. ;]
of a gloomy countenance: Mt 6:16, Lk 24:17.†

σκοτεινός.as:
σκοτεινός (WH. -τινός), -ή, -όν
(< σκότος), [in LXX chiefly for חֹשֶׁךְ and cogn. forms ;]
dark: opp. to φωτεινός, Mt 6:23, Lk 11:34, 36.†

σκότος.as:
σκότος, -ου, ὁ the more usual cl. form (cf. σ., τό),
darkness: He 12:18, Rec.†

σκύλλω.as:
* σκύλλω
1. in cl., to skin, flay, rend (Æsch., Anthol.).
2. In Hellenistic writers, to vex, trouble, annoy: c. acc. pers., Mk 5:35, Lk 8:49; pass., ἐσκυλμένοι, distressed, Mt 9:36; mid., to trouble oneself, μὴ σκύλλου, Lk 7:6 (freq. in π.; v. MM, i, ii, and cf. M, Pr., 89; Abbott, Essays, 87; Kennedy, Sources, 82).†

σκεῦος.g: a vessel to contain liquid, utensil, tackle
σκεῦος.long: a vessel to contain liquid; a vessel of mercy or wrath; any instrument by which anything is done; a household utensil; of ships: tackle.
σκεῦος.sd: a vessel, implement, equipment or apparatus (literally or figuratively [specially, a wife as contributing to the usefulness of the husband])
σκεῦος.as:
σκεῦος, -ους, τό
[in LXX chiefly for כְּלִי ;]
a vessel, implement (for exx. in various senses, v. MM, xxii): Mk 11:16, Lk 8:16, Jo 19:29, Ac 10:11, 1611:5, Ro 9:21, Re 18:12; pl., II Ti 2:20, Re 2:27; τὰ σ. τῆς λειτουργίας, He 9:21; pl., τὰ σ., utensils, goods, Mt 12:29, Mk 3:27, Lk 17:31; id. of the tackle or gear of a ship (Xen., Polyb., al.); so in sing., τὸ σ., Ac 27:17. Metaph., of persons: σ. ἐκλογῆς, Ac 9:15; ὀργῆς, Ro 9:22; ἐλέους, ib. 23; σ. εἰς τιμήν (cf. Ro 9:21), II Ti 2:21; of woman, ἀσθενέστερον σ., I Pe 3:7; so perh. τ. ἑαυτοῦ σ., I Th 4:4 (but v. infr.); of the body, II Co 4:7; so perh. I Th 4:4 (but v. supr., and v.s. κτάομαι).†

σκορπίζω.long: I disperse, scatter abroad (as of sheep); I dissipate, waste; I distribute alms.
σκορπίζω.sd: to dissipate, i.e. (figuratively) put to flight, waste, be liberal
σκορπίζω.der: apparently from the same as G4651 (σκορπίος) (through the idea of penetrating);
σκορπίζω.as:
σκορπίζω
[in LXX for פּוּץ hi., etc. ;]
in vernac. and in Ion, and late writers for σκεδάννυμι (v. MM, xxiii; Rutherford, NPhr., 295), to scatter: ὁ λύκος, Jo 10:12; ὁ μὴ συνάγων μετ’ ἐμοῦ σκορπίζει, Mt 12:30, Lk 11:23; pass., seq. εἰς, c. acc. loc., Jo 16:32; of one who dispenses blessings, II Co 9:9(LXX) (of. δια-σκορπίζομαι).†

σκάνδαλον.long: a snare, stumbling-block, cause for error.
σκάνδαλον.sd: a trap-stick (bent sapling), i.e. snare (figuratively, cause of displeasure or sin)
σκάνδαλον.kj: occasion to fall (of stumbling), offence, thing that offends, stumblingblock
σκάνδαλον.der: ("scandal"); probably from a derivative of G2578 (κάμπτω);
σκάνδαλον.as:
† σκάνδαλον, -ου, τό
(late form of the rare word σκανδάληθρον, v. LS, s.v.) [in LXX chiefly for מוֹקֵשׁ, מִכְשׁוֹל ;]
prop., the bait-stick of a trap, a snare, stumbling-block (Le 19:14, Jth 5:1): fig., Ro 9:33, I Pe 2:8 (Is 8:14; aliter in LXX; στερεὸν σκανδάλου in Aq.). Metaph., of that which causes error or sin;
(a) of persons: Mt 13:4116:23; Χριστὸς ἐσταυρωμένος, I Co 1:23;
(b) of things: Mt 18:7, Ro 11:9(LXX)14:13, I Jo 2:10Re 2:14; τὸ σ. τοῦ σταυροῦ, Ga 5:11; pl., Mt 18:7, Lk 17:1, Ro 16:17.†
SYN.: πρόσκομμα

σκηνή.long: a tent, booth, tabernacle, abode, dwelling, mansion, habitation.
σκηνή.sd: a tent or cloth hut (literally or figuratively)
σκηνή.der: apparently akin to G4632 (σκεῦος) and G4639 (σκιά);
σκηνή.as:
σκηνή, -ῆς, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for אֹהֶל, also for מִשְׁכָּן, סֻכָּה, etc. ;]
a tent, booth, tabernacle: Mt 17:4, Mk 9:5, Lk 9:33, He 11:9; αἱ αἰώνιοι σ., Lk 16:9; of the Mosaic tabernacle, He 8:59:2, 3, 6, 8, 21; σ. τ. μαρτυρίου, Ac 7:44; of its heavenly prototype, He 8:29:11, Re 13:615:521:3; of the temple, He 13:10; ἡ σ. τοῦ Μολόχ, Ac 7:43(LXX); metaph., ἡ σ. ΔαυείδAc 15:16(LXX).†

σκληροκαρδία.der: feminine of a compound of G4642 (σκληρός) and G2588 (καρδία);
σκληροκαρδία.as:
† σκληρο-καρδία, -ας, ἡ
(< σκληρός, καρδία), [in LXX: De 10:16, Je 4:4 (לֵבָבעׇרְלָה), Si 16:10 (cf. καρδίασκληρά, ib. 3:26, 27) * ;]
hardness of heart: Mt 19:8, Mk 10:516:[14].†

σκοτίζομαι.as:
† σκοτίζω
(< σκότος), [in LXX for חשׁךְ ;]
to darken; in NT always pass., -ομαι, to be darkened: of the heavenly bodies, Mt 24:29, Mk 13:24, Lk 23:45 (Rec., WH, mg.), Re 8:12. Metaph., of the mind, Ro 1:2111:10(LXX) (cf. σκοτόω).†

σκληρός.sd: dry, i.e. hard or tough (figuratively, harsh, severe)
σκληρός.as:
σκληρός, -ά, -όν
(< σκέλλω, to dry), [in LXX chiefly for קָשָׁה ;]
hard to the touch, rough, harsh, (opp. to μαλακός); metaph., in various uses;
(a) of men, hard, stern, severe: Mt 25:24;
(b) of things, hard, rough, violent: σκληρόν σοι (ἐστι), Ac 26:14; λόγος, Jo 6:60; ἄνεμος, Ja 3:4; σκληρὰ λαλεῖν, Ju 15.†
SYN.: αὐστηρός, q.v

σκώληξ.as:
σκώληξ, -ηκος, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for תּוֹלָע and cogn. forms ;]
a worm: of the kind which preys upon dead bodies, metaph., of fut. punishment, Mk 9:48 (LXX, Is 66:24; cf. Si 7:17, Jth 16:17).†

σκιρτάω.sd: to jump, i.e. sympathetically move (as the quickening of a fetus)
σκιρτάω.as:
σκιρτάω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Ge 25:22 (רצץ hithpo.), Ps 113 (114):4, 6 (רקד), etc. ;]
to leap: Lk 1:41, 446:23.†

σκολιός.as:
σκολιός, -ά, -όν
[in LXX: De 32:5 (עִקֵּשׁ), Pr 28:18 (σ. ὁδοῖς πορεύεσθαι, for: דְּרָכַיׅםנֶעֱקַשׁ), Is 40:4 (עָקֹב), etc. ;]
curved, bent, winding (opp. to ὀρθός, εὐθύς): Lk 3:5(LXX). Metaph., crooked, perverse, unjust: Ac 2:40, Phl 2:15, I Pe 2:18.†

σκάπτω.as:
σκάπτω
[in LXX: Is 5:6 (עדר ni.)* ;]
to dig: Lk 6:4813:816:3.†

σκορπίος.der: probably from an obsolete (perhaps strengthened from the base of G4649 (σκοπός) and meaning to pierce);
σκορπίος.as:
σκορπίος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX for עַקְרָב ;]
a scorpion: Lk 10:1911:12, Re 9:3, 5, 10.†

σκοπέω.long: I look at, regard attentively, take heed, beware, consider.
σκοπέω.sd: to take aim at (spy), i.e. (figuratively) regard
σκοπέω.kj: consider, take heed, look at (on), mark
σκοπέω.as:
** ακοπέω, -ῶ
(< σκοπός), [in LXX: Es 8:13, II Mac 4:5 * ;]
to look at, behold, watch, contemplate. Metaph., to look to, consider: c. acc. rei, II Co 4:13, Phl 2:4; c. acc. pers., Ro 16:17, Phl 3:17; seq. μή, Lk 11:35; σεαυτόν, seq. μή (v. M, Pr., 192), Ga 6:1 (cf. ἐπι-, κατα-σκοπέω).†
SYN.: βλέπω, θεωρέω, ὁράω

σκηνόω.g: I dwell as in a tent, encamp
σκηνόω.long: I dwell as in a tent, encamp, have my tabernacle.
σκηνόω.sd: to tent or encamp, i.e. (figuratively) to occupy (as a mansion) or (specially), to reside (as God did in the Tabernacle of old, a symbol of protection and communion)
σκηνόω.as:
σκηνόω, -ῶ
(< σκηνή), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁכֵן ;]
to have one's tabernacle, to dwell (in π. of temporary dwelling, v. MM, Exp., xxii): seq. ἐπί, c. acc. pers., Re 7:15; seq. ἐν, c. dat. pers., Jo 1:14; id. c. dat. loc., Re 12:1213:6; seq. μετά, c. gen. pers., Re 21:3 (cf. ἐπι-, κατα-σκηνόω).†

σκηνοπηγία.long: the feast of tabernacles, the great festival of the Jews, held in October.
σκηνοπηγία.sd: the Festival of Tabernacles (so called from the custom of erecting booths for temporary homes)
σκηνοπηγία.as:
σκηνοπηγία, -ας, ἡ
(< σκηνή, πήγνυηι), [in LXX for סֻכּוֺת, De 16:1631:10, Za 14:16, 18, 19; I Es 5:51, I Mac 10:21, II Mac 1:9, 18 * ;]
prop., the setting up of tents or dwellings (Arist.); in LXX and NT, ἡ σ., ἡ ἑορτή τῆς σ. (called also ἑορτὴ σκηνῶν, Le 23:34, al.; v. Deiss., LAE, 116 f.), the feast of Tabernacles: Jo 7:2.†

σκέλος.sd: through the idea of leanness); the leg (as lank)
σκέλος.as:
σκέλος, -ους, τό
[in LXX for רֶגֶל, etc. ;]
the leg from the hip downwards: Jo 19:31-33 †

σκήνωμα.long: a tent pitched, a dwelling, tabernacle.
σκήνωμα.sd: an encampment, i.e. (figuratively) the Temple (as God's residence), the body (as a tenement for the soul)
σκήνωμα.as:
σκήνωμα, -τος, τό
(< σκηνόω), [in LXX chiefly for אֹהֶל ;]
a tent, tabernacle (cf. σκηνή, σκῆνος): of the temple as God's dwelling (Ps 131 (132):5, al.), Ac 7:46. Metaph., of the body: II Pe 1:13, 14.†

σκληροτράχηλος.as:
† σκληρο-τράχηλος, -ον
(σκληρός, τράχηλος), [in LXX: Ex 33:3, 5 (עֹרֶף ־קָשֶׁה), etc. ;]
stiff-necked: metaph., Ac 7:51.†

σκωληκόβρωτος.der: from G4663 (σκώληξ) and a derivative of G977 (βιβρώσκω);
σκωληκόβρωτος.as:
* σκωληκό-βρωτος, -ον
(< σκώληξ, βιβρώσκω),
eaten of worms: Ac 12:23 (cf. II Mac 9:9, and v. MM, xxiii) †

σκηνοποιός.as:
*† σκηνοποιός, -όν
(< σκηνή, ποιέω),
making tents; as subst., ὁ σ., a tent-maker: Ac 18:3.†

σκληρύνω.long: I harden, make hard, make stubborn.
σκληρύνω.as:
σκληρύνω
(< σκληρός), [in LXX chiefly for קשׁה hi., also for חזק ;]
to harden. Metaph., to harden, make stubborn: c. acc. pers., Ro 9:18; τ. καρδίας (Ps 94 (95):8), He 3:8, 154:7. Pass., to become hardened: Ac 19:9, He 3:13.†

σκάφη.sd: a "skiff" (as if dug out), or yawl (carried aboard a large vessel for landing)
σκάφη.as:
** σκάφη, -ης, ἡ
(< σκάπτω), [in LXX: Da LXX Bel 32, TH ib. 33 * ;]
anything scooped out, esp. a light boat, skiff: Ac 27:16, 30, 32.†

σκευή.as:
** σκευή, -ῆς, ἡ
[in LXX: III Mac 5:45 R * ;]
equipment, tackle: Ac 27:19.†

σκληρότης.long: hardness, hardness of heart, obstinacy, perverseness.
σκληρότης.as:
σκληρότης, -ητος, ἡ
(< σκληρός), [in LXX: De 9:27 (קְשִׁי), etc. ;]
hardness; metaph., of stubbornness: Ro 2:5.†

σκῆνος.long: a tent, tabernacle; fig: of the human body.
σκῆνος.sd: a hut or temporary residence, i.e. (figuratively) the human body (as the abode of the spirit)
σκῆνος.as:
** σκῆνος, -ους, τό
[in LXX: Wi 9:15 * ;]
= σκηνή,
a tent, tabernacle (C.I., 3071). Metaph., of the body as the tabernacle of the soul: II Co 5:1, 4.†

σκόλοψ.long: a stake or thorn; fig: a sharp affliction.
σκόλοψ.sd: withered at the front, i.e. a point or prickle (figuratively, a bodily annoyance or disability)
σκόλοψ.der: perhaps from the base of G4628 (σκέλος) and G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι);
σκόλοψ.as:
σκόλοψ, -οπος, ὁ
[in LXX: Nu 33:55 (שֵׂךְ), Ho 2:6 (8) (סִיר), Ez 28:24 (סִלּוֹן), Si 43:19 * ;]
anything pointed, esp.
1. in cl., a stake
2. In Hellenistic vernacular, a thorn (cf. LXX, ll. c.): σ. τῇ σαρκί, II Co 12:7 (cf. MM, i., xxiii; DB, iii, 700 f.; Deiss., St. Paul, 62 f.; Field, Notes, 187).†

σκοτόομαι.sd: to obscure or blind (literally or figuratively)
σκοτόομαι.as:
σκοτόω, -ῶ
(< σκότος), [in LXX for חשׁךְ, קדר, שׁחר ;]
to darken: Re 9:216:10. Metaph., of the mind : pass., Eph 4:18 (cf. σκοτίζω).†

σκύβαλον.sd: what is thrown to the dogs, i.e. refuse (ordure)
σκύβαλον.der: neuter of a presumed derivative of G1519 (εἰς) and G2965 (κύων) and G906 (βάλλω);
σκύβαλον.as:
**† σκύβαλον, -ου, τό
[in LXX: Si 27:4 * ;]
refuse, esp. dung (v. MM, ii, iii, xxiii): Phl 3:8.†

σκοπός.long: a watcher; a goal, a mark aimed at.
σκοπός.sd: perhaps akin to G4626 (σκάπτω) through the idea of concealment; compare G4629 (σκέπασμα)); a watch (sentry or scout), i.e. (by implication) a goal
σκοπός.as:
σκοπός, -οῦ, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for צֹפֶה ;]
1.a watcher, watchman (Ez 3:17, al.).
2.a mark on which to fix the eye (Wi 5:12, 21, al.). Metaph., of an aim or object: Phl 3:14.†

Σκύθης.long: a Scythian, as typical of the uncivilized.
Σκύθης.sd: a Scythene or Scythian, i.e. (by implication) a savage
Σκύθης.as:
Σκύθης, -ου, ὁ
Scythian, an inhabitant of Scythia, i.e. Russia and Siberia, a synonym with the Greeks for the wildest of barbarians: Col 3:11.†

σκέπασμα.sd: perhaps akin to the base of G4649 (σκοπός) through the idea of noticeableness); clothing
σκέπασμα.as:
* σκέπασμα, -τος, τό
(< σκεπάζω, to cover),
a covering, esp. clothing: I Ti 6:8.†
